title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page has only three lines of blue-ink note, with the page number 266 at top right and archive folio 103. My best reading is: 'Cartier. — changt de connexion proj[ective] (or 'p-graduée'?) est vraiment simple [crossed out: devient] changer le … et … de l'opération'. The rest of the sheet is blank apart from show-through from the verso.

The neighbouring pages fix the context: projective connections on a curve X, presumably in characteristic p.
- The previous page writes c(s) for the horizontality condition of a section of the P-torsor attached to a projective connection. With a_1 = λ dt it obtains a Riccati equation, dλ/dt + λ² = A.
- The next page sets this up intrinsically. Sections of P-σ(X) are ordinary connections D on ω, and they form a torsor under ω. Each D determines a projective connection c_D, with the cocycle rule c_{D0+ω1} = c_{D0} + 2D0(ω1) + ω1². Horizontality of D0+ω1 for the projective connection c_{D0}+ϖ2 is then the Riccati equation 2D0(ω1) + ω1² = ϖ2.

This isolated remark is a reminder or aside. The 'Cartier operation' attached to a projective connection is presumably the p-curvature-type or Cartier-type operator, as in the title of cote 93. The remark says its behaviour under a change of projective connection c → c + q (q a quadratic differential) is 'really simple'. Grothendieck seems to mean that the change amounts to altering some ingredient ('le …') of the operation. Because the last line is illegible, the precise claim cannot be reconstructed.
errors: No checkable mathematics on the page; the statement is too fragmentary to verify.

ideas.what: Behaviour of the Cartier operation / p-curvature of projective connections under change of projective connection by a quadratic differential
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature of opers / projective connections in characteristic p (dormant opers, Cartier operator on curves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (p-curvature, ~1970); Ihara (Schwarzian equations in char p, 1970s); Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory, 1990s)

deep.surprise_reason: A three-line, largely illegible aside asserting that something about the Cartier operation is 'simple' under change of projective connection. The surrounding projective-connection/Riccati computations are classical, and no recoverable new result is present.
transcription_corrections: 'connexion p-graduée' is more plausibly 'connexion proj[ective]', matching the context of the adjacent pages; uncertain.
Second line: 'est vraiment simple', with the crossed-out word apparently 'devient', followed by 'changer le'.
Third line is mostly illegible; it ends with 'de l'opération'. Readings such as 'germe' are speculative.
